findings.title: PLAN closed rollout vocabulary omits the new reconciliation states
findings.requirement: Every versioned tuple coordinate must have one closed vocabulary shared by PLAN and the normative manifest.
evidence: PLAN.md:379 enumerates the rollout coordinate but omits WIDENING_RECONCILING and PROMOTION_RECONCILING.
docs/state-transition-manifests.md:675 and :705 use both values in reachability and reducer rules.
IC32-UW/UP/RWX/RPX/RN and IH01-W/P plus IH06-WX/WN/PX/PN use them as reachable rollout sources or targets.
findings.impact: A compiler using PLAN’s declared versioned coordinate rejects the round-9 effect-first states as unknown, while a compiler accepting the manifest has a different schema. The effect-first correction is therefore not reproducible from one exact contract.
findings.required_correction: Add both reconciliation values to PLAN §14.0’s closed rollout coordinate and any generated schema/vocabulary equality checks; require exact equality with the manifest vocabulary.

findings.title: Post-reconciliation rollback and cleanup rows omit required canonical adjacency
findings.requirement: Every synchronized tuple row must stutter or traverse only explicit §2 canonical adjacency, with the exact sequence stated.
evidence: Reconciliation rollout states project canonical BLOCKED under manifest :705.
IC32-RWX/RPX (:763-764) and IH06-WX/PX (:977,:979) change that tuple to rollback REQUESTED but state only ROLLBACK_REQUESTED; §2 has no BLOCKED->ROLLBACK_REQUESTED edge.
IC32-RN (:765) and IH06-PN (:980) state only CLEANING rather than the available explicit BLOCKED>CLEANING edge.
findings.impact: The manifest’s universal adjacency rule makes these round-9 continuation rows invalid or leaves their canonical transaction sequence undefined. Settled exposure/no-exposure after safe reconciliation can strand.
findings.required_correction: Give every row an exact legal §2 sequence. Add a justified canonical edge only if necessary; otherwise use the existing BLOCKED>CLEANING path and an explicit legal BLOCKED-to-rollback sequence, then cover each in tuple witnesses.

findings.title: Effect-first degradation has no row after a durable verified Effect but before rollout consumption
findings.requirement: Every active rollout degradation must atomically record degradation, fence progress, and choose one safe path without losing a reachable interleaving.
evidence: IR38 and IR18 require an already-durable direct E06 receipt, so E06 may settle the Effect while rollout remains WIDENING_EFFECT or PROMOTING.
IH01-W/P (:968,:970) match only when the original Effect is unsettled or exposure classification is not protected.
Generic IH01 excludes WIDENING_EFFECT and PROMOTING, and no other IH01 row handles the settled, protected-exposure interval.
findings.impact: Telemetry degradation in a reachable post-E06/pre-IR38-or-IR18 window has no legal control-health transition. Safety handling can block or race the success projection despite the claimed exhaustive degradation partition.
findings.required_correction: Either consume E06 and change rollout atomically, or add exact synchronized degradation rows for settled/protected X and N cases with one rollback or cleanup owner and legal canonical projections. Extend the exhaustive IH witness set.

findings.title: IC32 revocation is not total over every reachable rollout coordinate
findings.requirement: Candidate revocation must be partitioned by every reachable rollout coordinate and protected X/N/unsettled classification, without inferred deltas or duplicate rollback.
evidence: Manifest :1010 explicitly requires enumeration of every reachable rollout coordinate.
IC32 rows :754-765 omit reachable SHADOW_PASSED coordinates including CANARY_ABORTING, CANARY_ABORTED, and CANARY_ABORT_SETTLED with rollback active or settled.
They also omit exposure-bearing PROMOTION_PENDING_APPROVAL, APPROVED, and WIDENING_REVIEW coordinates; IC32-N cannot apply where a current ExposureReceipt exists.
findings.impact: A revocation arriving in these nonterminal coordinates cannot atomically revoke/fence through IC32, or would need a false no-exposure fact or duplicate rollback. This contradicts PLAN §8.4’s exact partition and leaves unsafe authority/cleanup behavior undefined.
findings.required_correction: Enumerate the omitted reachable coordinates with exact existing-rollback/no-new-rollback, protected exposure/no-exposure, stop/quiescence, rollout, cleanup-owner, and replay behavior. Make checker equality use the actual generated reachable coordinate set.

findings.title: IR34 and IR35 enter canary abort without an exact protected X/N classifier
findings.requirement: Every reachable canary abort entry must select and persist exactly one protected exposure or no-exposure classification that can satisfy IR13A or IR13B.
evidence: IR34 and IR35 (:816-817) move CANARY_READY to CANARY_ABORTING after the admitted child fails or cancels but do not persist an X or N branch classifier.
IR12 can then reach CANARY_ABORTED, where only IR13A or IR13B may settle.
The claimed exhaustive abort witness list at :1007 enumerates IR07/09/10/53 and IH01-C continuation but omits IR34/IR35.
findings.impact: These abort paths rely on an unstated later proof-producing transition and can strand at CANARY_ABORTED under the closed rows. The claim that every abort source has exactly one X/N row is false.
findings.required_correction: Split IR34 and IR35 into explicit reachable X/N rows or prove and record a protected no-exposure classifier atomically in each row. Add both paths to exact abort classification and IR13B witnesses.

findings.title: Reducer prose assigns all ROLLED_BACK cleanup to IRB08 despite the widening-abort exception
findings.requirement: The normative reducer must state one consistent, complete cleanup owner for each rollback_origin and cancellation coordinate.
evidence: Priority 7a (:691), IRB08 (:907), and :910 correctly forbid IRB08 for rollback_origin=WIDENING_ABORT and assign IR13C under cancellation NONE.

The terminal-resolution paragraph at :714 instead says a settled ROLLED_BACK ‘does not permanently mask cleanup’ because priority 7a preserves it ‘only until IRB08 changes cleanup NOT_REQUIRED->PENDING’.
That universal explanation has no widening-abort qualification.
findings.impact: Two normative reducer descriptions disagree about the sole transition out of ROLLED_BACK. A literal implementation either rejects widening-abort cleanup or illegally lets IRB08 bypass the origin partition.
findings.required_correction: Rewrite :714 to reproduce the exact origin/cancellation partition: IR13C for WIDENING_ABORT/NONE, IRB08 for non-WIDENING_ABORT/NONE, and IX03 for pending cancellation.

findings.title: IR13A and IR13C permit parent cleanup before rollback reaches ROLLED_BACK
findings.requirement: Exposed canary abort cleanup must start only after real rollback is fully settled at ROLLED_BACK, with IR13C as the later sole owner under cancellation NONE.
evidence: IR13A (:793) accepts rollback ‘verified/rolled-back’, which includes the declared rollback state VERIFIED.
IR13C (:795) requires the IR13A branch receipt and cancellation NONE but has no rollback_state=ROLLED_BACK guard.

Priority 7 (:690) still forces canonical ROLLBACK_VERIFIED at VERIFIED, so IR13C’s REVIEW>CLEANING projection cannot apply; :691, :910, and :1004 all state that the widening-abort tuple is ROLLED_BACK through IR13A before IR13C.
findings.impact: The rows either allow cleanup scheduling before IRB07 records the rollback outcome or make IR13C reject under the reducer. This breaks the exact exposed-abort settlement path and contradicts the round-9 cleanup-owner contract.
findings.required_correction: Require rollback_state=ROLLED_BACK in IR13A’s exposed branch and recheck it in IR13C. Keep IRB07 before IR13A, then prove the ROLLED_BACK-through-IR13A-to-IR13C sequence for NONE and the IX03 sequence for REQUESTED/QUIESCING.

residual_uncertainty: This was a plan-only static/table audit, not an implementation test, exhaustive generated reachable-product proof, or production-safety validation.
Legacy source content and semantic entailment were not revalidated; the package correctly leaves immutable retrieval and same-run human edge review as future gates.
